title: BluePeak x Redwood - Private deployment discovery
next_steps: Redwood to send a short write-up on 'no egress' / disconnected install assumptions
BluePeak to confirm whether any outbound to OCSP/CRL or external DNS is permitted
Schedule technical deep dive on on-prem packaging and upgrades
content:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-01-17
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 44 min
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood), Ben Carter (Redwood), Nina Shah (BluePeak), Tom Wilkes (BluePeak), Priya Menon (BluePeak)

Summary
BluePeak is interested in Redwood Private but requires the deployment to run without outbound internet access. Discussed what 'air gapped' means in their environment, artifact delivery, and upgrade cadence.

Transcript
Ava Chen: cool, thanks everyone. maybe we start with what you're trying to do and constraints?
Nina Shah: yeah. so we have a regulated environment. the big thing is, it's disconnected. no outbound internet. like, *no egress*.
Ben Carter: when you say no egress, do you mean no outbound from the k8s cluster at all, or just no outbound to public internet?
Tom Wilkes: effectively no outbound to the internet. we can do internal stuff. but we don't want the cluster talking out.
Ava Chen: got it. so if Redwood Private needs to pull images, we would need to mirror into your registry?
Tom Wilkes: yep. we have an internal registry. we can pre-load.
Priya Menon: and procurement wise, we also need to understand updates. we can't do like, auto update checks.
Ben Carter: right. our installer currently assumes it can pull charts and images unless configured. we do have override paths, but for totally disconnected we usually deliver a bundle.
Nina Shah: also the phrase air-gap gets thrown around. it's not fully offline in the sense of no network. it's just no outside network.
Ava Chen: ok. sometimes we hear 'air gapped' and it includes like no external DNS, no OCSP, no anything. does your security team allow outbound for certificate checks?
Nina Shah: no. we handle that internally.
Ben Carter: that's helpful. so we'd want to make sure no component calls home, telemetry, license checks, etc.
Ava Chen: we can disable telemetry in Private. we should document it.
Tom Wilkes: can you also clarify if your system needs outbound for time sync?
Nina Shah: internal NTP only.
Ava Chen: ok. and is this in your own data center or a VPC?
Tom Wilkes: on prem.
Ben Carter: cool. then the work is: offline artifacts, pinned image digests, and some docs.
Ava Chen: next steps, we'll send a write-up on what we need from you to validate 'no egress'. and we should schedule a deep dive with our packaging folks.
Nina Shah: sounds good.
